labeling_method.annotation_guidelines: Not explicitly documented; each LLM used its own interpretation

cv_generation.implication: CVs are synthetic, not real candidate resumes. This means the relevance judgments are about synthetic CV vs. real JD pairs.

inferred_criteria: Skills match between CV and JD

original_label_columns.relevant_resume_ids: List of resume IDs relevant to each job

evidence: Perfectly balanced seniority distribution (625 each for Jr/Mid/Sr/Lead)
Perfectly balanced industry distribution (100 each for 25 industries)

label_structure.unlabeled_pairs: All non-matched pairs are unlabeled (not confirmed negative)

relevance_definition.inferred_definition: A resume is 'relevant' to a job if it appears in the job's relevant_resume_ids list. The criteria for relevance are unknown.
relevance_definition.relevance_scope: Unknown (could be skill-based, role-based, or overall suitability)

indicators: Perfect balance in seniority across jobs and resumes
Perfect balance in industry across jobs and resumes
synthetic_assessment.implication: Both the data AND the match labels are likely synthetically generated. Labels may reflect rule-based matching (e.g., industry/seniority/skill overlap) rather than genuine human relevance judgments.

audit_table.original_definition: Median of 3 LLM relevance scores (Claude, GPToss, Llama)
audit_table.label_reliability: Partially verified (LLM consensus, no human validation)

audit_table.mapping_status: Conditional mapping (individual scores less reliable than consensus)

audit_table.original_definition: Resume is listed as relevant to job
audit_table.positive_definition: Resume ID appears in job's relevant_resume_ids
audit_table.mapping_status: Conditional mapping (positive → label ≥ 1, but grade unknown)

incompatibilities.description: Vietnamese uses continuous 1-9 scale (from LLM median). English uses implicit binary (present/absent in match list). These cannot be directly aligned.
incompatibilities.resolution: Map Vietnamese 1-9 to common 0-3 rubric via calibrated thresholds. Map English positives to common rubric using structured feature analysis.

incompatibilities.description: Vietnamese: multi-dimensional (skills + experience + education) with justifications. English: unknown criteria (possibly rule-based on metadata similarity).
incompatibilities.resolution: Use Vietnamese justifications to understand scoring criteria. For English, analyze matches to reverse-engineer matching criteria.

incompatibilities.description: Vietnamese: 4 LLM annotators with consensus mechanism and justifications. English: unknown annotation source with no quality assessment.
incompatibilities.resolution: Vietnamese labels have better provenance but still lack human validation. Both require human-validated test set.

incompatibilities.description: Vietnamese: real JDs from TopCV + synthetic CVs from LLM. English: both jobs and resumes appear fully synthetic.
incompatibilities.resolution: Document data provenance. Consider that model may learn different patterns from synthetic vs. semi-real data.

incompatibilities.type: Different definitions of positive and negative
incompatibilities.description: Vietnamese: explicit positive and negative pairs (above/below threshold). English: positive-only (no confirmed negatives). Absent pairs are unlabeled, not negative.
incompatibilities.resolution: Do not automatically assign label 0 to unlisted English pairs. Use PU-learning techniques or careful negative sampling.

incompatibilities.description: Vietnamese provides fine-grained 1-9 scores enabling graded relevance. English provides only binary (relevant/not-in-list) with no granularity.
incompatibilities.resolution: For the common rubric (0-3), Vietnamese can be mapped using score thresholds. English positives need scoring based on structured feature analysis.
